key_insight: An order-by-order high-frequency expansion reveals how pore-wall curvature, field gradients, and induced displacement flow shape porous-media response beyond the leading viscous and thermal characteristic lengths.
engineering_relevance: The framework can help interpret acoustic-response parameters in absorbing foams in terms of pore-size disorder and flow-path constrictions or enlargements.
method: Expand oscillatory Stokes flow and heat conduction in the thin-boundary-layer limit.
Solve recursive WKB-type transport equations with a non-secularity condition and a displacement-flow Neumann problem at each order.
Express higher-order parameters as wall integrals and connect them to relaxation-time spectral data.
evidence_signal: Application to parameters fitted on highly absorbing foams links a negative surface parameter to strong parallel pore-size disorder and a large positive third-order term to flow-path constrictions or enlargements.
watch_item: The expansion assumes high frequencies and thin boundary layers; isolated sharp edges introduce apparent parameters that vary logarithmically.
paper_title: Boundary Layers, Displacement Flow, and the High-Frequency Response of Porous Media: Beyond the Viscous and Thermal Characteristic Lengths, Order by Order
